response.text: Consumer fireworks may only be discharged in the City on Victoria Day or Canada Day, or on a day covered by a special occasions fireworks discharge permit issued by the Fire Chief [2]. You also cannot discharge consumer fireworks on land you do not own unless you have the owner's prior written consent [2], and you must keep fire extinguishing equipment ready at the site [2]. Consumer fireworks may be discharged in the City only on Victoria Day or Canada Day (or the next day before or after, if weather makes it impractical or unsafe), and not after 11:00 p.m. on those days [2]. On other days you need a special occasions fireworks discharge permit from the Fire Chief, and it can only be used on the date, time and location it specifies [3]. Discharging consumer fireworks is prohibited on any land other than your own without the owner's written consent [2]. Your own backyard therefore works only on those designated days or under a permit, and you must keep fire extinguishing equipment available [2]. Consumer fireworks may be discharged only on Victoria Day or Canada Day (or the next day before or after, if weather makes the designated day impractical or unsafe), and not after 11:00 p.m. on those days [2]. Discharge on any other day requires a special occasions fireworks discharge permit issued by the Fire Chief, and on the owner's land you may discharge only with the owner's consent if it is not your property [2][3]. Discharge is also barred within 100 metres of certain institutions such as schools, hospitals and religious institutions, unless written consent is obtained [3]. The passages do not state the times on days other than Victoria Day and Canada Day.

response.text: Partly. Automated vehicles are subject to the same laws as other vehicles, but many traffic and parking regulations assume a human driver, so tickets must be issued to a human driver. Owner liability, meaning a ticket issued to the vehicle owner, already exists for many non-moving violations such as parking, stopping and standing, and for red-light camera enforcement [3]. Moving violations are primarily governed by provincial legislation, and changes to enforcement authority or liability for fully driverless vehicles would require provincial consideration [3]. The City's authority over automated vehicles is limited and the City cannot override provincial enforcement provisions [4]. The documents do not say whether the City can ticket a driverless car for a moving violation.
